subject: Re: LSR-Encord Follow-up
text:
Hi Nick.

Quick question: Do you have experience where any of your clients have segmented the coronary arteries using a 3D cursor (as shown in the attached video) and then exported the data for fine-tuning in Encord?

Additionally, does your team have an opinion on whether segmenting cases purely in 2D from the get-go is faster and/or more reliable than segmenting in 3D, with or without fine-tuning in 2D?

We have several other CCTA studies in the pipeline.  The number of cases to process could become such that even small gains in efficiency could have a meaningful financial impact.

Lastly, do your labelers exclusively use Encord segmentation tools?  Or is there is a process whereby we teach your team to do preprocessing using a third-party tool prior to uploading it to Encord for refinement and approval?  There is no wrong answer; just curious.

Slicer is just one of several advanced tools that we use.  Several new, AI-enabled tools have come online that provide an excellent starting point for subsequent fine-tuning.  We are curious if there is model whereby we can get the best of both worlds with you platform and labeling team.

Perhaps we can discuss this further when we talk.

Nick

subject: RE: Encord contract
text:
Thanks, Nick M!

I have signed the agreement and look forward to receiving the countersigned version once Ulrik signs it.

Quick question: Since LSR will have a paid rather than a “freemium” license, may I assume that our data, including segmentation masks and images, will NOT be used for internal R&D.  Or, per Encord’s terms and conditions, should I formally opt-out of having our data used?  Some of our clients explicitly prohibit such use, including by LSR, so I must assure we remain compliant with our obligations.

Platform System Data. For Clients and users under a Freemium License, Encord may, as permitted under this Agreement use data generated through the Client’s use of the Service including, but not limited to vector embeddings, metadata, ontologies, and label specifications, for internal research and development to support certain product features and improve functionality within the Services. You may opt-out of having your data used for research and development purposes at any time by emailing: support@encord.com.

Also, the terms and conditions state that “Encord provides 250GB of included data storage via the Google Cloud Platform unless otherwise stated in the Agreement or in a Client’s Order Form.”  This is fairly limited storage for most medical imaging applications, so may I assume that this applies to ancillary storage rather than the typical storage required for most real-world segmentation projects?  We normally set aside half a terabyte for each client project involving CT imaging and ramp up from there.

I have accepted your meeting invitation for Monday.  Thanks so much!!  We’re excited to get going.

Have a great weekend.

Nick

Nicholas Wharton | President, LightSource Research

subject: Re: Encord & Oléa Médical
text:
Hello Skander,

I spent some time at the end of last week and went through the Encord documentation. The objective was to make a clear comparison between Redbrick and your products in terms of entities definitions and mapping.
It would be great to consider that as a basis of discussion for our next meeting (question answers to text in red).

[cid:image001.png@01DB761D.E69B53F0]

As mentioned, I’d like to emphase again that we spent a LOT of time implementing a complete custom SDK (based on Python Redbrick SDK) to automate data import and label import / export with Redbrick. Technically speaking, we’d want to first ensure that 100% of our needs would be covered by Encord before going any further. Setting up a system like this is time consuming and we’d need to gain from you both technical and commercial solid convictions to move forward.

In my opinion, we shall first make sure that you can address a clear methodology to import DICOM or NIFTI data from our s3 meaning => Patient, Study, Series, Instance levels in both DICOM and NIFTI formats and can get a clear view of the proposed workflow to be applied during the entire project life cycle (label import / export and versioning).
We also DO need to deeper dive into your medical imaging viewer which looks to have quite limited functionalities in terms of displaying 4D (multi-phases) series. This is a must have for our annotators.

Have a nice day,
Regards,
JF
